Kowalski leads a human-made aquarium tour, twice a day, to the trails at the San Francisco Bay “Beneath” tropical rainforests. Her goal is — and it’s been her motto to save the marine animals in the Health Bay, California area, basement ecosystems and corridors. She’s kicked off Project HUB as a Marine Protected Area on the ocean floor with two objectives: to collect specimens (packed bags are worth more, according to Dr. Kowalski) and distribute them in the Bay; and to help scientists around the world find solutions for coral bleaching.
Through a $117,000 grant from the National Science Foundation, Dr. Kowalski analyzes coral reef samples and compares them to satellite images and aircraft reporting levels. Unable to receive funding from the National Geographic Society, she turns to Dr. Jennifer Mason, the department of marine biology and ocean sciences at Tulane University. The office of the assistant professor of marine science features on her website and is a dynamic, self-sustaining experimental facility that fills a coral reserve every day, often from her intentions to provide the best algae care possible for the coral.
